explained with acorns

lines.text: Squirrel lost 35% of its acorns. Getting back takes 54%.
lines.say: Squirrel lost thirty-five percent. Getting back takes fifty-four.

lines.text: First, the words. Bull market: prices climb. Bear market: prices fall 20% or more from the top.
lines.say: First, the words. Bull market: prices climb. Bear market: prices fall twenty percent or more from the top.

lines.text: The S&P 500 has had 27 bear markets since 1928. Squirrel is not special.
lines.say: The S and P five hundred has had twenty-seven bear markets since nineteen twenty-eight. Squirrel is not special.

lines.text: The average bear lasted 289 days. The average bull lasted 988.
lines.say: The average bear lasted two hundred eighty-nine days. The average bull lasted nine hundred eighty-eight.

lines.text: Bears took 35% on average. Bulls added 112%.

lines.text: Now the sneaky part. 100 acorns fall 35% to 65 acorns.
lines.say: Now the sneaky part. A hundred acorns fall thirty-five percent, to sixty-five acorns.

lines.text: Getting back to 100 takes 35 more acorns. That's a 54% gain.
lines.say: Getting back to a hundred takes thirty-five more acorns. That's a fifty-four percent gain.

post.title: Bull vs bear markets, explained with acorns
post.ig:
Squirrel lost 35% of its acorns. Getting back takes 54%.

Bear market: down 20% or more from the last peak.
Average bear: 289 days, -35%. Average bull: 988 days, +112% (Hartford Funds).
The catch: a 35% drop needs a 54% gain to get back to even.
In April 2025 the S&P 500 fell 18.9%, just short of a bear.

Sources: Hartford Funds (S&P 500 since 1928), CNBC (Apr 2025).
News and education, not financial advice.

A bear market is a 20% drop from the last peak. Since 1928 the S&P 500 has had 27; the average bear lasted 289 days and fell 35%, while the average bull lasted 988 days and gained 112% (Hartford Funds). And a 35% drop needs a 54% gain to get back to even.
